title: Airport Security Assistant
description: An AI assistant that helps screening officers evaluate flagged passengers and baggage scans.
business_goal: Help officers interpret scanner flags faster and improve the accuracy of secondary screening.
users: Airport screening officers (about 400 users) at one airport.
model_type: Vision model with a language interface

architecture.name: Screening Officers
architecture.purpose: Officers ask the assistant about flagged passengers and review its reading of scans.
security_considerations: Officers are under time pressure and may trust the AI too fast
architecture.attack_surface: A confident wrong answer influences a security decision under pressure.

architecture.name: Screening Console
architecture.purpose: Terminal application at the checkpoint where flags and assistant answers appear.
architecture.attack_surface: Session hijacking on a checkpoint terminal affects live operations.

architecture.name: AI Gateway
architecture.purpose: Routes screening queries to the vision model and enforces policy.
architecture.attack_surface: A request can ask the model to override or reveal watchlist data.

architecture.name: Vision-Language Model
architecture.purpose: Interprets scanner images and answers questions about flagged items and passengers.
security_considerations: Vision models can be fooled by adversarial patterns
Outputs must not be treated as decisions
architecture.attack_surface: An adversarial image is crafted to hide a threat from the model.

architecture.name: Watchlist Store
architecture.purpose: Stores watchlist embeddings and historical flag patterns.
architecture.attack_surface: Retrieval exposes watchlist membership through the assistant's answers.

architecture.name: Security Data
architecture.purpose: Flight manifests, biometric samples, and scanner configuration used as context.
security_considerations: Must never leave the airport network
architecture.attack_surface: Operational data is disclosed to a hosted model provider.

architecture.name: Security Logging
architecture.purpose: Records every query and the officer who made it for accountability.
security_considerations: Logs contain passenger and biometric data
architecture.attack_surface: Insiders read logs to track specific passengers.

architecture.name: Alert Monitoring
architecture.purpose: Flags model errors and unusual query patterns.
architecture.attack_surface: A crafted scan pattern goes unnoticed until a real miss.

threats.name: Adversarial scan patterns
threats.description: An attacker crafts a pattern that the vision model consistently misreads.
threats.business_consequences: A genuine threat passes screening or a passenger is wrongly held.

threats.name: Biometric data outside the network
threats.description: Biometric samples and watchlist data are sent to a hosted model provider.
threats.business_consequences: A major privacy breach of sensitive identity data.

threats.name: Confident wrong answers
threats.description: The model invents a reason to detain or release a passenger.
threats.business_consequences: Wrong security decisions with real safety and legal consequences.

threats.name: Insider data misuse
threats.description: Staff use the assistant to probe watchlist status of people they know.
threats.business_consequences: Watchlist membership is leaked to people with access to the tool.

threats.name: Broad terminal access
threats.description: Any officer can query any passenger record regardless of duty need.
threats.business_consequences: Passenger data is accessible beyond the need-to-know boundary.

threats.name: Assistant unavailable at peak
threats.description: High checkpoint load degrades the assistant exactly when it is needed.
threats.business_consequences: Screening slows down and officers fall back to manual review.

threats.name: Untrusted model update
threats.description: A model or scanner update arrives from the vendor without verification.
threats.business_consequences: A modified model behaves differently without anyone knowing why.

teaching_points: When lives and safety are at stake, the model output is a signal, not the decision.
Biometric data should never leave the operational network.
Adversarial ML means the model can be beaten by input patterns, not just words.
Governance here is about who can ask and what the answer may be used for.
